Command: Pay a hired servant his wages on time
Summary: The wages of a hired servant are given him on his day, before the sun goes down: the day's pay is not held past the day it was earned.
Commandment: Pay a hired servant his wages on time.
Application: Prompt pay is the positive form of the labour law: the wage arrives when it is needed, at the day's end, because the labourer is poor and sets his heart upon it. Employers today owe the same promptness, whatever the pay period's form.
Purpose: Deuteronomy states the ground: the laborer depends on the day's pay (Deuteronomy 24:15); James warns withheld wages cry out (James 5:4). Here that ground requires paying wages on time.
Function: This is a civil law, setting the terms on which neighbours deal with each other. The wages of a hired servant are given him on his day, before the sun goes down. Deuteronomy states the ground: the labourer depends on the day's pay; James warns that withheld wages cry out against the one who kept them. The evil it addressed was a day's work kept unpaid while the worker went hungry. It restrained that evil by putting a deadline on the wage: pay arrives when it is needed, at the day's end, not when the master finds it convenient.
